clue.text: Stars in gold rush, endlessly pursuing bit of money

indicators.note: the gold-and-rush pieces chase, so come after, the coin piece

parts.note: a cent is a small coin, a bit of money
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: endlessly means the word rush loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A prospector in a gold rush, chasing every last cent, gazes at the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Centaurus is a southern constellation, a named group of stars.

clue.text: Distressed union in a hole

indicators.note: in means the union letters are placed inside the hole

parts.note: on a golf green the cup is the hole
TU stands for trade union

explanation.surface: A distressed trade union finds itself in a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut up is an idiom for upset or distressed.

clue.text: City's ruler looked down on by senior woman

indicators.note: in a down entry the grandmother sits above, so looks down on, the ruler

parts.note: nan is a grandmother, a senior woman
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A king is looked down on by an elderly woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanking, now Nanjing, is a major city in eastern China.

clue.text: Everyone wants short form of game to get multi-talented player

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: short form of means the game's name loses its last letter

parts.note: rounders is a British bat-and-ball game like baseball

explanation.surface: Everybody wants a shortened version of the game to suit a versatile player.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an all-rounder is skilled at both batting and bowling.

clue.text: Little woman in scarlet performed again

indicators.note: in places the short woman's name inside the colour

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
Di is a shortened form of Diana

explanation.surface: A little woman in scarlet gives an encore.
explanation.definitionFit: Redid is the past tense of redo: did once more.

clue.text: Dog hunts, craze seen to be bad, that finally gets banned

indicators.note: seen to be bad means the remaining letters go wrong and are reordered
gets banned means the selected letter is struck out of the fodder
finally picks the last letter of the word that

explanation.surface: A dog's hunting craze is judged bad and finally banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes T from 'that'; 'gets banned' removes it from HUNTS CRAZE, and 'seen to be bad' rearranges HUNSCRAZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A schnauzer is a German breed of wire-haired terrier-like dog.

clue.text: Automaton, companion making a hash of things

parts.note: a bot is a robot or automaton
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A robot sidekick who keeps messing everything up.
explanation.definitionFit: A botch is a clumsy, bungled job, which is what making a hash of something produces.

clue.text: Vehicle going over hard territory down under?

indicators.note: in a down entry the vehicle goes over, above, the next letter

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A vehicle crosses rough terrain in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia the bush is the wild rural back country, hence the down-under question mark.

clue.text: Interval for players performing in dull setting

indicators.note: in, with setting, places the performing word inside the dull word
setting means the dull word forms the surround for the other piece

parts.note: trite means hackneyed, dull
on means performing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: Musicians perform during an interval in a dreary venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tritone is a musical interval of three whole tones, as played by musicians.

clue.text: Husband, individual leading group, set up seductive scheme

indicators.note: leading means the individual comes before the group

parts.note: one means a single individual

indicators.note: set up in a down entry means the group's word is turned upwards, backwards

parts.note: a party is a group

explanation.surface: A husband, one who leads a group, is framed.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeytrap is a scheme using seduction to lure someone into a compromising position.

clue.text: Snarled up net, finally used rod and line

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word net

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line, so angled

explanation.surface: An angler's net and line become a knotted mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Snarled up and tangled both describe threads twisted into knots.

clue.text: A shine's possibly required for a boot

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of a shine's may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Polish is needed to make a boot gleam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required for' is link text: the anagram of A SHINE'S gives the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hessians are tall tasselled riding boots first worn by German soldiers from Hesse.

clue.text: Ancient men grabbed by old-maidish kisser

indicators.note: grabbed by means the soldiers' letters are held inside the other two pieces

parts.note: prim means prudish and old-maidish
dial is slang for the face, as is kisser
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Some ancient men are seized by a prudish spinster wanting a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Primordial means existing from the very beginning, hence extremely old.

clue.text: Hoax by Yankee showman

parts.note: cod as a verb or noun means a hoax or leg-pull
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American showman pulls off a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffalo Bill Cody ran the famous travelling Wild West show.

clue.text: Keep going, using computers in project

indicators.note: in places the computing letters inside the project verb

parts.note: to project is to stick out
IT, information technology, means computers

explanation.surface: Persevere with a project that uses computers.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick it out is an idiom for persevering to the end.

clue.text: One won't want milk, say, being kept in vehicle

indicators.note: being kept in puts the abbreviation for say within the vehicle

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
e.g. means for example, or say

explanation.surface: A milk float driver finds someone in the van who refuses milk.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan eats no animal products, dairy included, so refuses milk.

clue.text: Truthful vicar lied unexpectedly

indicators.note: unexpectedly means the letters come out in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: A vicar surprisingly told a lie, and the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Veridical is a formal word for truthful or corresponding to reality.

clue.text: Look always to keep dry dictionary?

indicators.note: to keep means the look and always pieces together hold the dry letters between them

parts.note: to gaze is to look
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always
TT, teetotal, means not drinking, dry

explanation.surface: Always looking up words while staying off the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazetteer is a geographical reference book listing places, a kind of dictionary of names, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Begin to run out of time for offering aid

definitions.text: Begin to run out of time
definitions.meaning: to fall behind schedule, starting to run out of time
a phrase for giving support; the answer is the verb, support, so the part of speech differs slightly

explanation.surface: Starting to run short of time to give help.
explanation.definitionFit: To get behind is both to fall behind schedule and to back or support a cause.

clue.text: Maybe Mirror reader backs football's decision-maker

indicators.note: backs means the reader comes behind the referee

parts.note: the referee, ref, makes the decisions in football
a lector reads lessons in church or lectures at a university

explanation.surface: A Daily Mirror reader supports the referee's call.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper, a misdirection: here it is a looking-glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirror is one example of a surface that reflects light.

clue.text: Short girl maybe hiding nothing, right? It's to do with what mini reveals!

definitions.text: to do with what mini reveals

indicators.note: hiding means the shortened word holds the next letters inside
Short means the last letter is dropped from the word for girl maybe

parts.note: a girl is an example of a female
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A short girl hiding nothing, all right, in a revealing miniskirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Femoral relates to the femur, the thigh bone, and a miniskirt shows the thighs.

clue.text: Mollusc served with soft pile of potatoes?

parts.note: a clam is a mollusc
p, piano, is the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: Clams served alongside a heap of mash.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamp is a mound of root crops stored under straw and earth for winter.

clue.text: Plant left with explosive carried by gangster repeatedly

indicators.note: carried by means the left and explosive letters are held inside the gangster pair
repeatedly means the gangster's name is written twice

parts.note: Al Capone was the notorious gangster
HE stands for high explosive

explanation.surface: A plant left with explosives carried by a gangster again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Allheal is a name for several herbs, such as valerian and self-heal, thought to cure all ills.

clue.text: Show the way, leading pair going to the back

indicators.text: leading pair going to the back
indicators.note: the leading pair of letters move to the back of the word for the way

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing

explanation.surface: Guides lead the way with a pair at the front then going to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is a demonstration, a show of how something works.

clue.text: Sale with silver being disposed of in palace

indicators.note: being disposed of means arranged differently, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: At a sale, the silver is got rid of in a palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Versailles is the vast royal palace near Paris built by Louis XIV.

clue.text: Something flowery appearing in early part of year, not November

indicators.note: not means the letter for November is left out

parts.note: spring is the early part of the year
November is N in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Something floral appears in spring, but not November.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small spray of a plant, often with flowers.

clue.text: Someone with halo certainly creating problems for viewers

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is pictured with a halo
yes means certainly

explanation.surface: A saint is certainly making trouble for TV audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Styes are inflamed swellings on the eyelid, problems for eyes, our viewers.

clue.text: Work interrupted by a sport

indicators.note: interrupted by means the letter A breaks into the work word

parts.note: to ply is to work at, as in ply a trade

explanation.surface: Work is disrupted by a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport and to play both mean to frolic or amuse oneself.

clue.text: Composer showing heart before bad turns

indicators.note: before puts the heart ahead of the following piece

parts.note: the core is the heart of something

indicators.note: turns means the word for bad is read backwards

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A composer reveals his heart before going bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcangelo Corelli was an Italian Baroque composer and violinist.

clue.text: Place for birds with eggs by railway, all right for nesting

indicators.note: for nesting means the all-right letters sit inside the eggs

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Birds nest with their eggs beside a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the railway after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookery is a colony of rooks, where many birds breed together.

clue.text: Sweet mint?

definitions.meaning: a lollipop or ice ..., a sweet on a stick
a mint is a vast sum of money

explanation.surface: A mint flavoured sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolly is British slang for cash, and a mint is a large amount of it; it is also a lollipop.

clue.text: Like a computer, is something that can be stimulating

parts.note: computers are digital machines

explanation.surface: A computer is described as something that can excite.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalis is a drug from foxglove that stimulates the heart muscle.
